Edit this record 83 lower-face mouth reference atlas into a restrained ANGRY speech atlas. Keep the exact 3x3 row-major layout A B C / D E F / G H X, grid/crop dimensions, facial identity, framing, skin, nose, cheeks, chin, jaw, neck, hair and background unchanged. Change only the mouth within each cell. Preserve the original muted brown lips, brown skin palette, original lip scale and soft pixel clusters. No red lipstick, orange skin, harsh contrast, bright white tooth flashes, extra tooth rows, or smile. Angry emotion comes from tense compressed lips, subtly tightened corners and downward mouth corners, while phonetic mouth family remains correct and all speech forms stay distinct.

Use these exact Rhubarb definitions:
A: Closed lips with light pressure, for P/B/M.
B: Slightly open, nearly together teeth; narrow horizontal opening, for most consonants and EE.
C: Medium open mouth with relaxed unrounded lips, for EH/AE.
D: Wide vertical opening for open AA; opening visibly larger than C.
E: Slightly rounded lips; opening no wider than C, for AO/ER.
F: Puckered rounded lips with a small forward opening, not a tooth bite, for UW/OW/W.
G: Upper teeth touch the lower lip; not a wide open vowel, for F/V.
H: Tongue raised behind upper teeth, opening between C and D; tongue may be subtle at this scale, for long L.
X: Closed relaxed idle lips, for silence.

Emotion and pose instructions: A is tensely pressed closed; B remains a narrow horizontal slit with teeth nearly together; C is a medium unrounded opening; D is a clearly wider vertical AA opening; E is a smaller rounded AO opening; F is a small rounded pucker with no teeth contact; G shows upper teeth meeting lower lip; H shows a long-L opening between C and D with raised tongue; X is closed relaxed idle. Keep lips anatomically small and original-sized. Do not alter anything outside mouth pixels. Return the edited atlas only, no labels or extra panels.
